speaker: abel_garnish
text: The margin is as I left it on Monday. Twenty-four lines. I have brought the pin, and I have not brought a fresh column. If you add nothing this morning, Master Kemp, the pin stays in the cork.

speaker: will_kemp
text: I shall add nothing out of a rehearsal. A yard is where a line earns its keep. You may write that I know the difference. You may not write that the difference flatters you.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Twenty-four stands. Nothing added, and no song. We are not rehearsing a comedy of lovers this morning, and we are not rehearsing a king. Egeon opens, and then Egeon waits. Do not shorten the wife to save the wait.

speaker: richard_burbage
text: The loss is the loss. Thou wilt not hurry it because a morning is short and an old man is long. I have said so of other endings. I will say it of this one, once.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Once is enough. The margin already has it. I am idle from the opening until the end. If the middle grows a clown while I am off the trestles, Abel will see it this afternoon, not this morning.

speaker: abel_garnish
text: This afternoon I will see what the yard hears. This morning I am looking at a book that already knows Monday. Eleven was Thursday. Thirteen was Monday. I am not going to add them again for the pleasure of a sum.

speaker: will_kemp
text: Twenty-four is the sum, and it is lines, and you will not marry it to a purse. I heard a man in the yard yesterday try. He failed, because I was standing on his sentence. You keep to you, Will. I am not your cousin this month, and I am not your debtor.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: You, then. And no debt of lines beyond the twenty-four, until a yard makes a new one. Dick, the brothers are not in this. The old man is not a pair of twins. Let the end find them without a wink from me in the middle.

speaker: richard_burbage
text: No wink. I would rather a clean wait than a clever one. Thou art good at clever, and the play is not asking for it between the first grief and the last.

speaker: abel_garnish
text: Two of the clock, the same part as Tuesday. I have no note of a chain, and no note of a door that went wrong, and I do not mean to acquire either before dinner. If a property is broken, it is broken in the world, not in my margin.

speaker: will_kemp
text: Nothing is broken except the patience of men who rehearse an opening they already know. I will be still in it. Still is not my fame. It is my manners, for one afternoon, and manners are not a song.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Manners will do. I was at the Theatre yesterday on a damp post, and I am not bringing the post here. No price came home with me. No one is to ask the price again in this parlour as if I had hidden it.

speaker: richard_burbage
text: My father has the post, and my brother has the question of who pays. Thou hast two mornings in March, which is Lent, and which is not this rehearsal. Leave Shoreditch on the north side where you left it.

speaker: abel_garnish
text: And leave Monday's thirteen where I wrote them. I will read them at the reckoning if anyone's memory has kindly shrunk them. It happens. I do not take it personally. I take it with the pin.

speaker: will_kemp
text: Read them. Twenty-four. If you read thirty-five you are reading Shrove Tuesday before it has come, and I will say so, in a loud voice, with you still in it.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Nobody is reading thirty-five. Shrove Tuesday is not today. Today is Egeon, slow at the loss, idle in the middle, present at the end. That is the whole of my part, and I will not decorate it to feel employed.

speaker: richard_burbage
text: Then we are fit to stop. I have the brothers in my mouth for the afternoon, and I do not want Egeon's grief still in their jokes. Go and eat, Will. Thou hast a letter somewhere that is older than this rehearsal.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: The letter is at the lodging, folded, and it goes to the Bell after we have played. I am not opening it in a tiring-parlour to see if Sunday still agrees with Thursday.

speaker: abel_garnish
text: Sunday can agree with itself. I agree with the margin. Twenty-four. No song. I will not say it a fourth time. Master Kemp, if you are a growing concern, grow after two of the clock, where I can count.

speaker: will_kemp
text: After two of the clock I shall be a man who knows when to be quiet in another man's shipwreck. You may bow to that, or you may save your bow. I am going to find something to eat that is not a cue.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Eat, then. The wife is not shortened. The tally is not grown. I will see you on the trestles, and I will not see you in the margin before then.

speaker: richard_burbage
text: And thou wilt not teach the opening to the afternoon while we are still in the morning. Once through, slow, and then dinner. I will not hear Egeon's grief twice before two of the clock.

speaker: abel_garnish
text: Once through is what I came for. The pin stays in the cork until the yard. If the middle grows a line while you are off the trestles, I will still be the man who hears it.

speaker: will_kemp
text: If the middle grows a line, it will grow where they paid, not where you are hungry. I have said I will be still. Still does not improve by being rehearsed into a speech.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Then stop. Slow at the loss, quiet in the middle, twenty-four in the margin. I am going home for the letter, and I am not taking the book to improve it over bread.
